result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility crosswalks and a marked bike lane, but is dominated by heavy vehicle traffic and wide crossing distances. A large dump truck significantly obstructs sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic at the primary crossing point.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large dump truck is positioned immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, completely blocking the view of pedestrians for approaching drivers and vice versa.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground at the crosswalk entrance

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without a median or refuge island.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The street environment features high-visibility crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and a dedicated bike lane, providing essential infrastructure for non-motorized users. However, the multi-lane roadway lacks physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions or a median, which increases pedestrian exposure during the crossing.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a physical refuge island, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Large vehicle occlusion
hazards.description: The presence of large trucks in the travel lanes can create significant blind spots between pedestrians and other drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, a marked zebra crosswalk, and a green bike lane, though it is currently impacted by a road closure and construction activity. The environment lacks visible pedestrian-specific signals and is dominated by large industrial-style buildings, which may affect pedestrian comfort and perceived safety.

hazards.name: Construction Zone
hazards.description: Road closure signage and orange barrels indicate active or pending construction, which can create unpredictable traffic patterns and temporary obstacles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway and along the curb line

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible at this signalized intersection, increasing the risk of crossing conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection corners near traffic light poles

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a two-lane industrial street with a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the environment lacks signals, signage, or traffic calming measures, which may lead to high vehicle speeds and increased exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: There is no signalized control at the marked crosswalk, forcing pedestrians to judge traffic gaps manually.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection of the crosswalk and the roadway

hazards.name: Wide lane geometry
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway in an industrial setting likely encourages higher vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway through the center of the image

hazards.name: Heavy vehicle presence
hazards.description: Large industrial trucks are present, which have larger blind spots and pose a higher risk in collisions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing lights to increase driver yielding rates at the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility warning signs to alert drivers to the upcoming pedestrian crossing.
